Reason: Figure 1b demonstrates a marked shift of the mediastinum and cardiac silhouette into the right hemithorax with an abnormal cardiac contour, which is characteristic of right-sided cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect following pneumonectomy or major pleural surgery. This mechanical displacement causes acute haemodynamic compromise by kinking the great vessels and impairing venous return.
